findings.current: If I didn’t want to get beaten to death, I’d make up things that never happened and tell you.
findings.defect: The conditional is logically inverted: inventing information would increase the speaker’s risk of being beaten rather than prevent it.
findings.rationale: The replacement restores the intended sarcastic logic without changing the exchange’s voice or timing.
findings.replacement: If I wanted to get beaten to death, I’d make up things that never happened and tell you.
findings.source: Chapter 490, Taekyung questioning a guard about Jeok Cheongang

findings.current: The Water God Dragon’s spirit has departed, but its enormous corpse is being dismantled and distributed under Taekyung’s direction.
findings.defect: The packet shows the corpse being dismantled and preliminary shares being negotiated, but no completed or ongoing distribution. Recording distribution as current fact advances the state beyond Chapter 494.
findings.rationale: This preserves the completed events while preventing the checkpoint state from introducing an unsupported development.
findings.replacement: The Water God Dragon’s spirit has departed, but its enormous corpse is being dismantled under Taekyung’s direction; distribution has not yet been completed.
findings.source: Checkpoint summary, Continuity bullet for the Water God Dragon’s corpse

findings.current: For all that time—long enough for the mountains and rivers to change four times—he had lived as a medical apprentice.
findings.defect: Calling Mungyeong a medical apprentice conflicts with the established Divine Physician identity and with the immediately following account of independently examining and treating thousands of patients.
findings.rationale: “Physician” maintains the established role and fits the medical experience described in the next sentence.
findings.replacement: For all that time—long enough for the mountains and rivers to change four times—he had lived as a physician.
findings.source: Chapter 494, Mungyeong reflecting on his forty years away from Murim

findings.current: Of course, along with cool water, it contained a deadly poison called Seven-Step Soul-Chasing Powder—an extreme poison that killed its victim before they could take seven steps.
findings.defect: The narration names the poison as Seven-Step Soul-Chasing Powder, but the immediately following System panel identifies this dose as Potent Seven-Step Soul-Chasing Powder, the distinct established term used in the checkpoint state.
findings.rationale: Using the full established name keeps the narration, System notification, summary, and durable state consistent.
findings.replacement: Of course, along with cool water, it contained a deadly poison called Potent Seven-Step Soul-Chasing Powder—an extreme poison that killed its victim before they could take seven steps.

findings.current:
> - Status abnormality: **Severe Stomachache**!
> - Status abnormalities will return to normal once you have fully recovered, but decreased abilities cannot be restored!
findings.defect: The System switches from the established term “Status condition,” used in Chapter 490, to “Status abnormality” for the same category of effect.
findings.rationale: Consistent System vocabulary prevents an incidental label change from implying a different mechanic.
findings.replacement:
> - Status condition: **Severe Stomachache**!
> - Status conditions will return to normal once you have fully recovered, but decreased abilities cannot be restored!

summary: Five actionable issues: one inverted joke, one premature continuity claim, one identity/role drift, and two System terminology inconsistencies.
